title.en: Volume 150 Biographies 100: Dezong's and Shunzong's Sons

sentences.zh: 孔巢父孔巢父，冀州人，字弱翁。

translations.literal: Kong Chaofu, Kong Chaofu, was a man of Jizhou; his style was Ruoweng.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu, whose courtesy name was Ruoweng, came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父如珪，海州司戶參軍，以巢父贈工部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Ru Gui was a registrar in the Haizhou revenue office; because of Chaofu he was posthumously granted Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru Gui had served as registrar in the Haizhou revenue office; Chaofu's later honors earned him a posthumous appointment as director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 巢父早勤文史，少時與韓準、裴政、李白、張叔明、陶沔隱於徂來山，時號「竹溪六逸」。

translations.literal: Chaofu early devoted himself to letters and history; in youth he withdrew to Mount Culai with Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Li Bai, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Min, and at the time they were called the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek."
translations.idiomatic: From an early age Chaofu immersed himself in literature and history. As a young man he retired to Mount Culai with Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Li Bai, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Min, a group then known as the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek."

sentences.zh: 永王璘起兵江淮，聞其賢，以從事辟之。

translations.literal: When Prince Yong Li Lin raised troops in the Jiang-Huai region, hearing of his worth he summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yong Li Lin raised an army in the Jiang-Huai region, he heard of Chaofu's reputation and recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 巢父知其必敗，側身潛遁，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chaofu knew he would certainly be defeated, turned aside and slipped away in secret, and thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu foresaw that the prince's cause was doomed, slipped away in secret, and thereby won a reputation for discernment.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，李季卿為江淮宣撫使，薦巢父，授左衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era Li Jiqing was Commissioner for Pacification of the Jiang-Huai; he recommended Chaofu, who was appointed Left Guard Army Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangde reign Li Jiqing, serving as commissioner for pacification of the Jiang-Huai region, recommended Chaofu, who was appointed registrar in the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，澤潞節度使李抱玉奏為賓幕，累授監察御史，轉殿中、檢校庫部員外郎，出授歸州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era the Zelu military commissioner Li Baoyu memorialized him for the staff, and he was repeatedly appointed Supervising Censor, then transferred to Palace Censor, Acting Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent out as prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali reign the Zelu military commissioner Li Baoyu brought him onto his staff. He rose through supervising censor, palace censor, and acting director in the Ministry of Revenue, and was eventually posted out as prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 建中初，涇原節度留後孟皞表巢父試秘書少監，兼御史中丞、行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era the acting Jingyuan military commissioner Meng Hao memorialized Chaofu for probationary Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and army march marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign the acting Jingyuan commissioner Meng Hao recommended Chaofu as probationary vice director of the Secretariat, with concurrent posts as vice censor-in-chief and army march marshal.

sentences.zh: 尋拜汾州刺史，入為諫議大夫，出為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Fenzhou, entered the capital as Remonstrance Counselor, and went out as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Fenzhou, recalled to the capital as remonstrance counselor, and then sent out again as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未行，會普王為荊襄副元帥，以巢父為元帥府行軍司馬，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before he departed, it happened that Prince Pu was made deputy commander-in-chief of Jing-Xiang; Chaofu was made march marshal of the commander's headquarters, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the Hunan post, Prince Pu was named deputy commander-in-chief for Jing-Xiang, and Chaofu was appointed march marshal at the command headquarters with the concurrent title of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋屬涇師之難，從德宗幸奉天，遷給事中、河中陜華等州招討使。

translations.literal: Soon came the disaster of the Jing troops; he followed Dezong to Fengtian, was promoted to Attendant-in-Attendance, and made Pacification Commissioner for Hezhong, Shan, Hua, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhou mutiny broke out, he accompanied Dezong to Fengtian and was promoted to attendant-in-attendance and pacification commissioner for Hezhong, Shan, Hua, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 累獻破賊之謀，德宗甚賞之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented plans for defeating the rebels, and Dezong greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted plan after plan for defeating the rebels, and Dezong held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 尋兼御史大夫，充魏博宣慰使。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Censor-in-Chief and appointed Commissioner to Console Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor-in-chief and dispatched as imperial commissioner to console Weibo.

sentences.zh: 巢父博辯多智，對田悅之眾，陳逆順利害君臣之道，士眾欣悚喜抃，曰：「不圖今日復睹王化！」

translations.literal: Chaofu was broadly eloquent and full of strategy; facing Tian Yue's troops he set forth the principles of rebellion and loyalty, advantage and harm, and the way of ruler and minister; the soldiers were delighted and awed, clapping their hands, saying: "We never thought we would see the king's transforming influence again today!
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu was eloquent and resourceful. Addressing Tian Yue's troops, he expounded the rights and wrongs of rebellion, the interests at stake, and the duties of ruler and subject. The soldiers were moved to joy and awe, clapping their hands and crying, "We never dreamed we would live to see the civilizing rule of the throne again!

sentences.zh: 及就宴，悅酒酣，自矜其騎射之藝、拳勇之略，因曰：「若蒙見用，無堅不摧。」

translations.literal: When they came to the banquet, Yue, flushed with wine, boasted of his horsemanship and archery and his prowess in boxing, and said: "If I am employed, nothing strong will I fail to crush."
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet Tian Yue, growing drunk, boasted of his skill in horsemanship and archery and his prowess in hand-to-hand combat, and declared, "Put me to use and no fortress will stand before me."

sentences.zh: 巢父謂之曰：「若如公言而不早歸國者，但為一好賊耳。」

translations.literal: Chaofu said to him: "If, as you say, you do not return to the state early, you are only a fine bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu replied, "If you truly possess such power yet still refuse to return to allegiance, you are nothing but an accomplished rebel."

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「為賊既曰好賊，為臣當作功臣。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "If as a bandit I am called a fine bandit, as a minister I ought to be made a meritorious minister."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue answered, "If a rebel may be called an accomplished rebel, then as a loyal minister I ought to be made a meritorious servant of the throne."

sentences.zh: 巢父曰：「國方有虞，待子而息。」

translations.literal: Chaofu said: "The state is just now in peril; it waits for you to bring peace."
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu said, "The empire is still in peril; it waits for you to restore peace."

sentences.zh: 悅起謝焉。

translations.literal: Yue rose and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue rose and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 悅背叛日久，其下厭亂，且喜巢父之至。

translations.literal: Yue had rebelled for a long time; his subordinates were weary of disorder and moreover rejoiced at Chaofu's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue had been in rebellion for years; his men were weary of the turmoil and welcomed Chaofu's arrival.

sentences.zh: 數日，田承嗣之子緒以失職怨望，因人心之搖動，遂構謀殺悅，而與大將邢曹俊等稟命於巢父。

translations.literal: After several days Tian Chengsi' son Xu, resentful over loss of office, took advantage of the wavering of men's hearts and thereupon plotted to kill Yue, and with the great general Xing Caojun and others reported to Chaofu for orders.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Tian Chengsi's son Xu, bitter over being stripped of office, exploited the shifting loyalties of the troops to plot Tian Yue's murder, then sought Chaofu's approval together with the senior general Xing Caojun and others.

sentences.zh: 巢父因其眾意，令田緒權知軍務，以紓其難。

translations.literal: Chaofu, following the will of the masses, ordered Tian Xu to act provisionally in military affairs to ease the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the mood of the army, Chaofu authorized Tian Xu to assume provisional command of military affairs and thereby defuse the crisis.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，李懷光擁兵河中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan Li Huaiguang held troops at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xingyuan reign Li Huaiguang held the Hezhong region with his army.

sentences.zh: 七月，復以巢父兼御史大夫，充宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Chaofu was again made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and appointed Commissioner to Console.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chaofu was again named censor-in-chief and dispatched as imperial commissioner to console the troops.

sentences.zh: 既傳詔旨，懷光以巢父嘗使魏博，田悅死於帳下，恐禍及。

translations.literal: After the edict was proclaimed, Huaiguang, because Chaofu had once been sent to Weibo and Tian Yue had died under his tent, feared disaster would reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict was read aloud, Huaiguang recalled that Chaofu had previously been sent to Weibo and that Tian Yue had died in his camp; he feared the same fate awaited him.

sentences.zh: 又朔方蕃渾之眾數千，皆在行列，頗驕悖不肅。

translations.literal: Moreover several thousand men of the Shuofang Fan and Hun tribes were all in the ranks, quite arrogant and insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Shuofang tribal troops from the Fan and Hun peoples were also in the ranks, unruly and insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 聞罷懷光兵權，時懷光素服待命，巢父不止之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Huaiguang's military authority was to be removed, at the time Huaiguang was in plain dress awaiting orders, but Chaofu did not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that Huaiguang was to be stripped of command, the troops grew restive even though Huaiguang himself stood in plain dress awaiting orders, and Chaofu did nothing to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 眾鹹忿恚，咄嗟曰：「太尉盡無官矣！」

translations.literal: The masses all were indignant and exclaimed: "The Grand Marshal has completely lost his offices!
translations.idiomatic: The men erupted in fury, shouting, "The Grand Marshal has been stripped of every office!

sentences.zh: 方宣詔，喧噪，懷光亦不禁止，巢父、守盈並遇害。

translations.literal: Just as the edict was being proclaimed there was uproar; Huaiguang also did not forbid it, and Chaofu and Shouying were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the uproar as the edict was being read, Huaiguang made no move to stop the violence, and both Chaofu and Shouying were killed.

sentences.zh: 上聞之震悼，贈尚書左僕射，仍詔收河中日備禮葬祭。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was shaken and grieved, posthumously granted him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and still ordered that within Hezhong he be buried and sacrificed to with full rites on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply shaken and grieved. He posthumously appointed Chaofu left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and ordered that his body be recovered in Hezhong and buried with full ceremonial honors on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 賜其家布帛米粟甚厚，仍授子正員官。

translations.literal: His family was granted cloth, silk, rice, and grain in great abundance, and his son was still given a regular-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his family lavish gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain, and conferred a regular-rank office on his son.

sentences.zh: 從子戡、戣、戢。

translations.literal: His nephews were Kan, Wei, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews were Kong Kan, Kong Wei, and Kong Ji.

sentences.zh: 戡，巢父兄岑父之子。

translations.literal: Kan was the son of Chaofu's elder brother Cenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kan was the son of Chaofu's elder brother Cenfu.

sentences.zh: 方嚴有家法，重然諾，尚忠義。

translations.literal: Upright and stern, he had household discipline, valued keeping promises, and esteemed loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and stern, he maintained strict household discipline, prized his word, and held loyalty and righteousness above all.

sentences.zh: 盧從史鎮澤潞，辟為書記。

translations.literal: When Lu Congshi held Zelu he summoned him as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Congshi governed Zelu he recruited Kan as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 從史浸驕，與王承宗、田緒陰相連結，欲效河朔事以固其位。

translations.literal: Congshi gradually grew arrogant, secretly connected himself with Wang Chengzong and Tian Xu, and wished to imitate the Hebei-Shandong precedent to secure his position.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi grew increasingly arrogant, secretly aligned himself with Wang Chengzong and Tian Xu, and sought to emulate the independent warlords of Hebei and Shandong to secure his own position.

sentences.zh: 戡每秉筆至不軌之言，極諫以為不可，從史怒戡，歲餘，謝病歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Whenever Kan took up the brush and came to improper words he remonstrated to the utmost that they could not be done; Congshi was angry with Kan, and after more than a year Kan pleaded illness and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kan drafted language he judged improper, he remonstrated forcefully that it must not stand. Congshi grew angry with him, and after more than a year Kan pleaded illness and retired to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫鎮揚州，召為賓佐。

translations.literal: When Li Jifu governed Yangzhou he summoned him as a staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu governed Yangzhou he summoned Kan to his staff.

sentences.zh: 從史知之，上疏論列，請行貶逐。

translations.literal: Congshi learned of it, submitted a memorial setting forth the case, and requested that he be demoted and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi learned of the appointment, memorialized the court with accusations, and demanded Kan's dismissal and banishment.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不得已，授衛尉丞，分司洛陽。

translations.literal: Xianzong had no choice and appointed him Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, with duties at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong had no choice but to appoint Kan vice director of the Imperial Stud with duties at the Luoyang branch court.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元中籓帥誣奏從事者，皆不驗理，便行降黜。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenyuan era when military commissioners falsely memorialized against their staff, none was investigated on the merits and demotions were carried out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenyuan reign, when a military commissioner falsely accused a staff member, the court never investigated the charge on its merits and simply ordered an immediate demotion.

sentences.zh: 及戡詔下，給事中呂元膺執之，上令中使慰喻元膺，制書方下。

translations.literal: When Kan's edict came down, Attendant-in-Attendance Lü Yuanying held it fast; the emperor ordered a palace envoy to console and instruct Yuanying, and only then was the decree issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict demoting Kan was issued, attendant-in-attendance Lü Yuanying blocked it. The emperor sent a palace envoy to reason with Yuanying, and only then was the decree allowed to proceed.

sentences.zh: 戡不調而卒，贈駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: Kan died without taking up his post, and was posthumously granted Acting Director in the Imperial Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: Kan died before he could take up the new post and was posthumously granted acting director in the Imperial Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 戣，字君嚴。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Junyan.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei, whose courtesy name was Junyan.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，鄭滑節度使盧群辟為從事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; the Zheng-Hua military commissioner Lu Qun summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, after which the Zheng-Hua military commissioner Lu Qun recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 群卒，命戣權掌留務，監軍使以氣淩之，戣無所屈降。

translations.literal: When Qun died, Wei was ordered to act in charge of remaining affairs; the army supervisory commissioner bullied him with his airs, but Wei would not yield or submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qun died, Wei was left in charge of administrative affairs. The army supervisory commissioner tried to intimidate him, but Wei refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 入為侍御史，累轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Attending Censor and was repeatedly transferred among directors in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as attending censor and rose through successive posts in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元和初，改諫議大夫，侃然忠讜，有諫臣體。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was changed to Remonstrance Counselor, upright and loyal in remonstrance, with the bearing of a remonstrating minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he was appointed remonstrance counselor, forthright and loyal in his criticisms, with the bearing of a true remonstrating official.

sentences.zh: 上疏論時政四條，帝意嘉納。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing four items of current policy, and the emperor's mind was pleased to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne on four points of current policy, and the emperor received his recommendations favorably.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，內官劉希光受將軍孫璹賂二十萬貫，以求方鎮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year the inner palace official Liu Xiguang received a bribe of two hundred thousand strings of cash from the general Sun Zuan to seek a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year the palace eunuch Liu Xiguang accepted a bribe of two hundred thousand strings of cash from the general Sun Zuan in exchange for securing a military governorship.

sentences.zh: 事敗，賜希光死。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Xiguang was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, the emperor ordered Liu Xiguang executed.

sentences.zh: 時吐突承璀以出軍無功，諫官論列，坐希光事出為淮南監軍使。

translations.literal: At the time Tutu Chenghuan, because his expedition had achieved no merit, was criticized by remonstrance officials and, implicated in the Xiguang affair, was sent out as army supervisory commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Tutu Chenghuan, whose military campaign had failed to achieve its aims, came under criticism from the remonstrance officials and, implicated in the Xiguang affair, was sent out as army supervisory commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 太子通事舍人李涉知上待承璀意未衰，欲投匭上疏，論承璀有功，希光無事，久委心腹，不宜遽棄。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's Communications Aide Li She, knowing the emperor's regard for Chenghuan had not waned, wished to submit a memorial through the complaint box arguing that Chenghuan had merit, Xiguang was innocent, he had long been entrusted as a confidant, and ought not to be abruptly cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Li She, communications aide to the crown prince, saw that the emperor's favor toward Chenghuan had not faded and prepared a memorial for the complaint box arguing that Chenghuan had rendered real service, that the Xiguang affair was no grounds for dismissal, and that a long-trusted confidant ought not be cast aside so abruptly.

sentences.zh: 戣為匭使，得涉副章，不受，面詰責之。

translations.literal: Wei was commissioner of the box; he received She's duplicate draft, would not accept it, and in person interrogated and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner of the complaint box, Wei intercepted She's duplicate draft, refused to accept it, and confronted him with a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 涉乃進疏於光順門。

translations.literal: She thereupon submitted the memorial at the Guangshun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li She then submitted the memorial directly at the Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 戣極論其與中官交結，言甚激切。

translations.literal: Wei argued to the utmost that he was in league with inner officials; his words were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Wei denounced him in the strongest terms for colluding with palace eunuchs, his language fierce and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 詔貶涉為陜州司倉。

translations.literal: An edict demoted She to granary officer of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li She demoted to granary officer of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幸臣聞之側目，人為危之。

translations.literal: Favored ministers heard of it and looked askance; people considered him in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites glared at him in resentment, and observers feared for his safety.

sentences.zh: 戣高步公卿間，以方嚴見憚。

translations.literal: Wei walked tall among dukes and ministers and was feared for his uprightness and severity.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held his head high among the highest ministers, and his uprightness and severity inspired fear.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太子侍讀，遷吏部侍郎，轉左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Reader to the Crown Prince, was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made concurrent reader to the crown prince, promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, and then transferred to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，信州刺史李位為州將韋嶽讒譖於本使監軍高重謙，言位結聚術士，以圖不軌。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Xinzhou prefect Li Wei was slandered by the prefectural officer Wei Yue to the circuit commissioner and army supervisory commissioner Gao Chongqian, who said Wei had gathered occultists to plot sedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Xinzhou prefect Li Wei was denounced by a local officer, Wei Yue, to the circuit commissioner and army supervisory commissioner Gao Chongqian, who accused Wei of gathering occult practitioners to plot sedition.

sentences.zh: 追位至京師，鞫於禁中。

translations.literal: Wei was summoned to the capital and examined within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was summoned to the capital and interrogated inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 戣奏曰：「刺史得罪，合歸法司按問，不合劾於內仗。」

translations.literal: Wei memorialized: "When a prefect is guilty, he ought to be returned to the legal offices for investigation; it is not fitting to impeach him before the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei memorialized: "When a prefect stands accused, the case belongs in the regular judicial offices. It is improper to try him before the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 乃出付御史臺。

translations.literal: He was then sent out and handed over to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The case was transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 戣與三司訊鞫，得其狀。

translations.literal: Wei together with the Three Offices examined and interrogated him and obtained the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei joined the Three Offices in the investigation and established the facts.

sentences.zh: 位好黃老道，時修齋箓，與山人王恭合煉藥物，別無逆狀。

translations.literal: Wei was fond of the Way of Huang-Lao, at the time practiced fasting and talismanic rites, and with the mountain man Wang Gong jointly refined medicines; there was no other sign of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was a devotee of Huang-Lao teachings who practiced ritual fasting and, together with the recluse Wang Gong, compounded elixirs. There was no evidence of sedition.

sentences.zh: 以嶽誣告，決殺。

translations.literal: Because Yue had falsely accused him, he was executed by decision.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue was executed for making a false accusation.

sentences.zh: 貶位建州司馬。

translations.literal: Wei was demoted to military adjutant of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was demoted to military adjutant of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時非戣論諫，罪在不測，人士稱之。

translations.literal: At the time, but for Wei's remonstrance, the guilt would have been beyond reckoning; scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Had Kong Wei not intervened, Li Wei might have faced an unpredictable fate. Men of learning praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 愈為中官所惡，尋出為華州刺史、潼關防禦等使。

translations.literal: He was hated by inner officials; soon he went out as prefect of Huazhou and Tong Pass defense commissioner, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs came to resent him, and he was soon posted out as prefect of Huazhou and Tong Pass defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and was changed to Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Court of Judicial Review and then appointed rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 十二年，嶺南節度使崔詠卒，三軍請帥，宰相奏擬皆不稱旨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Lingnan military commissioner Cui Yong died; the three armies requested a commander, and the chief ministers' nominations all failed to please the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Lingnan military commissioner Cui Yong died. The army petitioned for a new commander, but none of the chief ministers' nominees satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 因入對，上謂裴度曰：「嘗有上疏論南海進蚶菜者，詞甚忠正，此人何在，卿第求之。」

translations.literal: When he entered for audience the emperor said to Pei Du: "There was once one who memorialized on the Nanhai tribute of oyster dishes; his words were very loyal and upright. Where is this man? You simply seek him out.
translations.idiomatic: During an audience the emperor said to Pei Du, "Someone once memorialized against the Nanhai tribute of oysters and clams in language notably loyal and forthright. Find that man for me.

sentences.zh: 度退訪之。

translations.literal: Du withdrew and made inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du withdrew and made inquiries.

sentences.zh: 或曰祭酒孔戣嘗論此事，度征疏進之。

translations.literal: Someone said Rector Kong Wei had once discussed this matter; Du sought out the memorial and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone identified Rector Kong Wei as the author of that memorial. Pei Du located the document and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 即日授廣州刺史，兼御史大夫、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: That very day he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Lingnan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Kong Wei was appointed prefect of Guangzhou with concurrent titles as censor-in-chief and Lingnan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戣剛正清儉，在南海，請刺史俸料之外，絕其取索。

translations.literal: Wei was upright, correct, pure, and frugal; in the Nanhai he requested that beyond the prefect's salary all exactions be ended.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, incorruptible, and frugal, he governed the Nanhai region and abolished every levy beyond the prefect's official salary.

sentences.zh: 先是帥南海者，京師權要多托買南人為奴婢，戣不受托。

translations.literal: Earlier those who commanded the Nanhai had many powerful men in the capital entrust them to buy southerners as male and female slaves; Wei would not accept such entrustments.
translations.idiomatic: Previous commanders of the south had routinely accepted commissions from powerful families in the capital to purchase southerners as slaves. Kong Wei refused every such request.

sentences.zh: 至郡，禁絕賣女口。

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery he forbade and ended the sale of women.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post he banned the sale of women outright.

sentences.zh: 先是準詔禱南海神，多令從事代祠。

translations.literal: Earlier, in accordance with edict to pray to the Nanhai god, many had their aides perform the sacrifice in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when an edict required prayers to the Nanhai sea god, commanders usually sent a subordinate to perform the rites in their place.

sentences.zh: 戣每受詔，自犯風波而往。

translations.literal: Whenever Wei received the edict he personally braved wind and waves to go.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kong Wei received such an edict he went in person, braving wind and waves.

sentences.zh: 韓愈在潮州，作詩以美之。

translations.literal: Han Yu was in Chaozhou and composed a poem to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, then in Chaozhou, composed a poem in his praise.

sentences.zh: 時桂管經略使楊旻、桂仲武、裴行立等騷動生蠻，以求功伐，遂至嶺表累歲用兵。

translations.literal: At the time the Guiguan frontier commissioner Yang Min, Gui Zhongwu, Pei Xingli, and others stirred up the raw barbarians to seek merit through campaigns, so that in the Ling region troops were used year after year.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Guiguan frontier commissioners Yang Min, Gui Zhongwu, Pei Xingli, and others provoked unrest among the indigenous peoples to win military glory, keeping the Lingnan region at war for years on end.

sentences.zh: 唯戣以清儉為理，不務邀功，交、廣大理。

translations.literal: Only Wei governed by purity and frugality, did not strive to invite merit, and brought great order to Jiao and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei alone governed through integrity and frugality, sought no glory through military campaigns, and brought peace and good order to Jiao and Guang.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne Kong Wei was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，或告戣在南海時家人受賂，上不之責，改右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Changqing era someone reported that while Wei was in the Nanhai his family had accepted bribes; the emperor did not hold him responsible and changed him to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing reign someone reported that Kong Wei's family had accepted bribes while he governed the south. The emperor did not hold him accountable but transferred him to right regular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 累請老，詔以禮部尚書致仕，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement; an edict made him Minister of Rites with retirement from office, and a gracious edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned for retirement and was granted the post of minister of rites with permission to retire, accompanied by an edict of warm praise.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司歲致羊酒，如漢禮征士故事。

translations.literal: He was still ordered that the relevant offices each year present sheep and wine, as in the Han ritual precedent for summoning scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered the relevant offices to present him with sheep and wine each year, following the Han dynasty precedent for honoring retired scholars.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年正月卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Changqing he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the fourth year of Changqing, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子遵孺、溫裕，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zunru and Wenyü both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zunru and Wenyü both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中已後，叠居顯職。

translations.literal: After the Dazhong era they repeatedly held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong reign they rose repeatedly to eminent offices.

sentences.zh: 溫裕位京兆尹、天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Wenyü reached the posts of Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao and Tianping military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü served as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 遵孺子緯，自有傳。

translations.literal: Zunru's son Wei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zunru's son Wei is the subject of a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 戢，字方舉，戣母弟也。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Fangju, was Wei's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji, whose courtesy name was Fangju, was Kong Wei's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 以季父巢父死難，德宗嘉其忠，詔與一子正員官，因授戢修武尉。

translations.literal: Because his younger uncle Chaofu had died in loyal service, Dezong commended his loyalty and ordered that one son be given a regular-rank office; Ji was thereby appointed Wei of Xiüwu.
translations.idiomatic: Because his uncle Chaofu had died in loyal service to the throne, Dezong commended the family's devotion and decreed that one son receive a regular-rank office; Kong Ji was appointed captain of Xiüwu.

sentences.zh: 以長兄戡未仕，固乞回授。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Kan had not yet taken office, he firmly begged that it be transferred back.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Kan had not yet received an appointment, he petitioned that the honor be transferred to him instead.

sentences.zh: 舉明經登第，判入高等，授秘書省校書郎、陽翟尉，入拜監察御史，轉殿中，分司東都。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination, was judged to enter the upper grade, was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat and magistrate of Yangdi, entered as Supervising Censor, was transferred to Palace Censor, and served at the eastern capital branch.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination with a high evaluation, was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat and magistrate of Yangdi, entered the capital as supervising censor, was promoted to palace censor, and served at the Luoyang branch court.

sentences.zh: 時昭義節度判官徐玟，以狡慝助成從史之惡。

translations.literal: At the time the Zhaoyi military commissioner's aide Xu Min, by craft and wickedness, helped bring Congshi's evils to completion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Min, a staff officer under the Zhaoyi military commissioner, had used his cunning to help Lu Congshi carry out his worst schemes.

sentences.zh: 從史既得罪，孟元陽為昭義節度，復欲用玟為賓佐，戢遂牒澤潞收玟以俟命，然後列狀上聞，竟流玟播州。

translations.literal: After Congshi had been punished, Meng Yuanyang became Zhaoyi military commissioner and again wished to employ Min as a staff adviser; Ji thereupon sent a dispatch to Zelu to seize Min and await orders, then submitted a report to the throne, and in the end Min was banished to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Congshi's downfall, Meng Yuanyang became Zhaoyi military commissioner and sought to bring Xu Min back onto his staff. Kong Ji dispatched orders to the Zelu authorities to detain Xu Min pending imperial decision, then memorialized the throne, and Xu Min was ultimately banished to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 轉侍御史、庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor and Acting Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor and acting director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，涇師之亂，硃泚署彭偃為舍人。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the disorder of the Jing troops, Zhu Ci appointed Peng Yan as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingzhou mutiny, Zhu Ci had appointed Peng Yan as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 至是偃子充符為鄜坊從事，或薦其才，執事者召至京師。

translations.literal: At this time Yan's son Chongfu was an aide in Fufang; someone recommended his talent, and those in charge summoned him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yan's son Chongfu was serving as an aide in Fufang. When someone recommended his talents, the authorities summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戢謂京兆尹裴武曰：「硃泚為偽詔，指斥乘輿，皆彭偃之詞也。

translations.literal: Ji said to the Metropolitan Prefect Pei Wu: "When Zhu Ci issued false edicts and reviled the imperial carriage, all were Peng Yan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji said to Metropolitan Prefect Pei Wu, "When Zhu Ci issued forged edicts denouncing the emperor, every word was Peng Yan's handiwork.

sentences.zh: 悖逆之子，不能鳥竄獸伏，乃違道以幹譽，子盍效季孫行父之逐莒仆，以勉事君者。」

translations.literal: The son of a rebel cannot hide like birds in flight or beasts in burrows, yet violates the Way to seek reputation; why do you not imitate Ji Sun Xingfu's expulsion of Ju Pu to encourage those who serve the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: The son of a traitor ought to hide in shame, not court favor by improper means. Why not follow Jisun Xingfu's example in expelling Ju Pu, and thereby encourage those who would serve the throne faithfully?

sentences.zh: 武即日逐充符。

translations.literal: Wu that very day expelled Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wu expelled Chongfu that same day.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹，出為汝州刺史、大理卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Metropolitan Prefect, went out as prefect of Ruzhou and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, then posted out as prefect of Ruzhou and director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 出為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時兄戣為嶺南，兄弟皆居節鎮，朝野榮之。

translations.literal: At the time his elder brother Wei was in Lingnan; the brothers both held military commands, and court and countryside honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his elder brother Kong Wei governed Lingnan, and with both brothers holding frontier commands the court and the public regarded them with admiration.

sentences.zh: 入為右散騎常侍，拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered as Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and was appointed Metropolitan Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right regular attendant of the cavalry and appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時累月亢旱，深軫聖情。

translations.literal: At the time drought had lasted for months, deeply troubling the sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: A prolonged drought had deeply troubled the emperor.

sentences.zh: 戢自禱雨於曲池，是夕大雨。

translations.literal: Ji himself prayed for rain at Qu Pond; that evening great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji prayed for rain at Qu Pond in person, and that evening a heavy downpour fell.

sentences.zh: 文宗甚悅，詔兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Wenzong was greatly pleased and ordered him concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong was greatly pleased and appointed him concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 大和三年正月卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Taihe he died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the third year of Taihe and was posthumously appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 子溫業，登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Wenye passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wényè passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中後，歷位通顯。

translations.literal: After the Dazhong era he successively held eminent and prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong reign he rose to a series of eminent offices.

sentences.zh: 溫業子晦。

translations.literal: Wenye's son was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wényè's son was Hui.

sentences.zh: 許孟容許孟容，字公範，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Xu Mengrong, Xu Mengrong, styled Gongfan, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mengrong, whose courtesy name was Gongfan, came from Chang'an in the Jingzhao metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 父鳴謙，究通《易象》，官至撫州刺史，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Mingqian thoroughly mastered the Images of the "Changes," reached the post of prefect of Fuzhou, and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mingqian was a master of the Images of the "Book of Changes" who rose to prefect of Fuzhou and was posthumously appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 孟容少以文詞知名，舉進士甲科，後究《王氏易》登科，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Mengrong early was renowned for literary composition; he passed the jinshi in the top grade, later studied Wang Bi's "Changes" and passed the examination, and was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong won early fame for his literary talent, passed the jinshi in the top grade, later mastered Wang Bi's commentary on the "Changes" and passed a further examination, and was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙贊為荊、襄等道黜陟使，表為判官。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zan was Commissioner for Promotion and Demotion of Jing, Xiang, and other circuits, he memorialized him as a judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zan served as commissioner for promotion and demotion in the Jing and Xiang circuits, he recommended Mengrong as his judge.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，徐州節度使張建封辟為從事，四遷侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan the Xuzhou military commissioner Zhang Jianfeng summoned him as an aide, and he was four times promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign the Xuzhou military commissioner Zhang Jianfeng recruited him as an aide, and he was promoted four times to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 李納屯兵境上，揚言入寇。

translations.literal: Li Na stationed troops on the border and proclaimed he would invade.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na massed troops on the border and threatened invasion.

sentences.zh: 建封遣將吏數輩告諭，不聽。

translations.literal: Jianfeng sent several generals and officials to announce and instruct him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng sent several officers to reason with him, but Li Na would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 於是遣孟容單車詣納，為陳逆順禍福之計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Mengrong alone in a single carriage to visit Na and set forth plans of rebellion and loyalty, disaster and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then sent Mengrong alone in a single carriage to Li Na's camp to expound the consequences of rebellion and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 納即日發使追兵，因請修好。

translations.literal: Na that very day sent envoys to recall his troops and thereupon requested restoration of friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na immediately recalled his troops and sent envoys to seek a renewal of friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 遂表孟容為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized Mengrong as prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na then memorialized the court to appoint Mengrong prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 無幾，德宗知其才，征為禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long Dezong knew his talent and summoned him as Acting Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dezong recognized his ability and summoned him to the capital as acting director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有公主之子，請補弘文、崇文館諸生，孟容舉令式不許。

translations.literal: A princess's son requested appointment as a student in the Hongwen and Chongwen halls; Mengrong cited the regulations and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: A princess's son petitioned for admission as a student in the Hongwen and Chongwen halls. Mengrong cited the regulations and refused.

sentences.zh: 主訴於上，命中使問狀。

translations.literal: The princess complained to the emperor, who ordered a palace envoy to inquire into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The princess complained to the emperor, who sent a palace envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 孟容執奏，竟得遷本曹郎中。

translations.literal: Mengrong held fast in memorializing and in the end was promoted to Director in his own bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong held firm in his memorial and was eventually promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 德宗降誕日，禦麟德殿，命孟容等登座，與釋、老之徒講論。

translations.literal: On Dezong's birthday he proceeded to Linde Hall, ordered Mengrong and others to ascend the dais, and debated with Buddhist and Daoist masters.
translations.idiomatic: On Dezong's birthday he held court in Linde Hall and had Mengrong and others take the dais to debate Buddhist and Daoist masters.

sentences.zh: 十四年，轉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed he was promoted to Attendant-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was promoted to attendant-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 十七年夏，好畤縣風雹傷麥，上命品官覆視，不實，詔罰京兆尹顧少連已下。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventeenth year Haozhi County suffered wind and hail that damaged the wheat; the emperor ordered ranked officials to re-inspect, found it untrue, and decreed punishment for the Metropolitan Prefect Gu Shaolian and those below.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventeenth year wind and hail damaged the wheat crop in Haozhi County. The emperor sent ranked officials to verify the report, found it false, and ordered punishments for Metropolitan Prefect Gu Shaolian and his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 敕出，孟容執奏曰：「府縣上事不實，罪止奪俸停官，其於弘宥，已是殊澤。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued Mengrong held it and memorialized: "When prefectures and counties report matters untruly, the crime extends only to confiscation of salary and suspension from office; as to broad pardon, that is already an extraordinary grace.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued Mengrong blocked it and memorialized: "When prefectural and county officials file false reports, the proper penalty is salary confiscation and suspension from office. Even that would already be an act of extraordinary clemency.

sentences.zh: 但陛下使品官覆視後，更擇憲官一人，再令驗察，覆視轉審，隱欺益明。

translations.literal: But after Your Majesty has ranked officials re-inspect, further select one censorial official and again order verification; with repeated inspection and re-examination, concealed deception becomes ever clearer.
translations.idiomatic: After Your Majesty sends ranked officials to verify the report, appoint one censorial official to investigate again. With successive reviews, any concealment or deception will become all the clearer.

sentences.zh: 事宜觀聽，法歸綱紀。

translations.literal: Matters ought to be observed and heard; the law returns to discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The matter should be examined openly, and the law should be upheld.

sentences.zh: 臣受官中謝日，伏請詔敕有須詳議者，則乞停留晷刻，得以奏陳。

translations.literal: On the day I received office and gave thanks at court I humbly requested that when edicts and decrees require detailed deliberation, I beg to detain them for a moment so that I may memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: When I took office I humbly requested that whenever an edict required careful deliberation, I be allowed a brief delay to present my views.

sentences.zh: 此敕既非急，宣可以少駐。」

translations.literal: This decree is not urgent and ought to be held briefly.
translations.idiomatic: This decree is not urgent and ought to be held briefly for review.

sentences.zh: 詔雖不許，公議是之。

translations.literal: The edict was not granted, but public opinion approved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his objection, but public opinion sided with Mengrong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，浙江東道觀察使裴肅卒，以攝副使齊總為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Zhejiang East Circuit observation commissioner Pei Su died; the acting deputy commissioner Qi Zong was made prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Zhejiang East Circuit observation commissioner Pei Su died, and the acting deputy commissioner Qi Zong was appointed prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 時總為肅剝下進奉以希恩，遽授大郡，物議喧然。

translations.literal: At the time Zong had stripped subordinates to send tribute seeking favor and was abruptly granted a great commandery; public opinion was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zong had extorted tribute from subordinates to curry imperial favor and was abruptly given a major prefecture, provoking widespread outrage.

sentences.zh: 詔出，孟容執奏曰：「陛下比者以兵戎之地，或有不獲已超授者。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued Mengrong held it and memorialized: "Your Majesty recently, in regions of military conflict, sometimes had no choice but to grant extraordinary promotions.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued Mengrong blocked it and memorialized: "Your Majesty has recently granted extraordinary promotions only in regions torn by warfare, where no alternative existed.

sentences.zh: 今衢州無他虞，齊總無殊績，忽此超授，群情驚駭。

translations.literal: Now Quzhou has no other concerns, Qi Zong has no special merit, yet suddenly this extraordinary appointment has startled and alarmed the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou faces no special threat, and Qi Zong has no distinguished record. This sudden extraordinary promotion has shocked the entire court.

sentences.zh: 總是浙東判官，今詔敕稱權知留後，攝都團練副使，向來無此敕命。

translations.literal: Zong was a judge of Zhedong; now the edict calls him acting provisional commissioner and acting deputy commander of the united training circuit—there has never been such a decree before.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zong was merely a staff judge in Zhedong, yet this edict names him acting provisional commissioner and acting deputy commander of the united training circuit—titles never before granted in such circumstances.

sentences.zh: 便用此詔，尤恐不可。

translations.literal: To use this edict as it stands is especially to be feared as impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To issue this edict as written would be especially unwise.

sentences.zh: 若總必有可錄，陛下須要酬勞，即明書課最，超一兩資與改。

translations.literal: If Zong truly has merit to record and Your Majesty must reward him, then clearly write his performance evaluation and promote him one or two grades in rank.
translations.idiomatic: If Qi Zong truly deserves reward, let Your Majesty record his achievements in writing and promote him one or two ranks by regular procedure.

sentences.zh: 今舉朝之人，不知總之功能，衢州浙東大郡，總自大理評事兼監察御史授之，使遐邇不甘，兇惡騰口。

translations.literal: Now everyone at court does not know Zong's capabilities; Quzhou is a great commandery of Zhedong, and Zong is appointed to it from Grand Court Evaluator concurrently Supervising Censor, making near and far unwilling and the vicious raise their voices.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court knows nothing of Qi Zong's abilities. Quzhou is a major prefecture of Zhedong, yet he is appointed from the lowly rank of grand court evaluator with concurrent supervising censor—a promotion that will outrage men near and far and give the malicious cause to speak out.

sentences.zh: 如臣言不切，乞陛下暫停此詔，密使人聽察，必賀聖朝無私。

translations.literal: If my words are not to the point, I beg Your Majesty temporarily to halt this edict and secretly send someone to listen and observe; all will surely congratulate the holy court on its lack of partiality.
translations.idiomatic: If my words miss the mark, I beg Your Majesty to suspend this edict temporarily and send someone to investigate in secret. The realm will surely applaud the court's impartiality.

sentences.zh: 今齊總詔謹隨狀封進。」

translations.literal: The present edict concerning Qi Zong is respectfully enclosed and forwarded with this report.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully enclose the edict concerning Qi Zong with this memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋有諫官論列，乃留中不下。

translations.literal: Soon remonstrance officials set forth arguments, and it was retained at court and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Soon other remonstrance officials joined the debate, and the edict was held at court and never issued.

sentences.zh: 德宗召孟容對於延英，諭之曰：「使百執事皆如卿，朕何憂也。」

translations.literal: Dezong summoned Mengrong to audience in Yanying and instructed him: "If all the hundred officials were like you, what would I have to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned Mengrong to audience in Yanying Hall and told him, "If every official were like you, what would I have to fear?".

sentences.zh: 自給事中袁高論盧杞後，未嘗有可否，及聞孟容之奏，四方皆感上之聽納，嘉孟容之當官。

translations.literal: Since Attendant-in-Attendance Yuan Gao's discussion of Lu Qi there had never been approval or rejection; when they heard Mengrong's memorial, all four quarters were moved by the emperor's willingness to accept remonstrance and praised Mengrong's fulfillment of office.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuan Gao's remonstrance against Lu Qi, the court had rarely seen such forthright approval or rejection of policy. When Mengrong's memorial became known, the realm was moved by the emperor's willingness to heed criticism and praised Mengrong for fulfilling his duty.

sentences.zh: 十九年夏旱，孟容上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year there was summer drought; Mengrong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year a summer drought struck, and Mengrong submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，物議嘉之。

translations.literal: Though the matter was not carried out, public opinion commended it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the proposal was not adopted, public opinion praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，坐裴延齡、李齊運等讒謗流貶者，動十數年不量移，故因旱歉，孟容奏此以諷。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan those who because of Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and others' slander were banished in exile often went more than ten years without measured transfer; therefore, taking advantage of drought and poor harvest, Mengrong memorialized this as admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan reign, officials exiled through the slanders of Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and their allies often went more than ten years without a transfer of posting. Mengrong used the drought and poor harvest as an occasion to offer this implicit admonition.

sentences.zh: 然終貞元世，罕有遷移者。

translations.literal: Yet to the end of the Zhenyuan era there were rarely any transfers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the remainder of the Zhenyuan reign, few exiles were ever transferred.

sentences.zh: 孟容以諷諭太切，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: Because Mengrong's admonition was too sharp, he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Because his admonition had been too pointed, Mengrong was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷刑部侍郎、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Justice and right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜京兆尹，賜紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Metropolitan Prefect and granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and granted the purple robe of high rank.

sentences.zh: 神策吏李昱假貸長安富人錢八千貫，滿三歲不償。

translations.literal: The Shence Army clerk Li Yu borrowed eight thousand strings of cash from a wealthy man of Chang'an and after three full years did not repay.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, a clerk in the Shence Army, borrowed eight thousand strings of cash from a wealthy Chang'an merchant and failed to repay it after three years.

sentences.zh: 孟容遣吏收捕械系，克日命還之，曰：「不及期當死。」

translations.literal: Mengrong sent officials to arrest and shackle him, set a day by which he must repay, and said: "If you do not meet the deadline you shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong sent officers to arrest and imprison him, set a deadline for repayment, and declared, "Miss the deadline and you die.

sentences.zh: 自興元已後，禁軍有功，又中貴之尤有渥恩者，方得護軍。

translations.literal: Since Xingyuan, those of the imperial guard who had merit, and especially those among inner favorites who had received thick favor, could protect army men.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xingyuan reign, only imperial guardsmen with distinguished service—or those under the protection of especially favored palace eunuchs—could shield their men from the law.

sentences.zh: 故軍士日益縱橫，府縣不能制。

translations.literal: Therefore soldiers daily grew more unrestrained, and prefectures and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the guardsmen grew ever more lawless, and the metropolitan and county authorities could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 孟容剛正不懼，以法繩之，一軍盡驚，冤訴於上。

translations.literal: Mengrong was upright and unafraid, restrained them by law, and the whole army was startled and pleaded their grievance to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong, upright and fearless, applied the law without flinching. The entire army was stunned, and they appealed to the emperor with grievances.

sentences.zh: 立命中使宣旨，令送本軍，孟容系之不遣。

translations.literal: Immediately the emperor ordered a palace envoy to proclaim the decree and command that he be sent to his original army; Mengrong kept him shackled and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately sent a palace envoy with orders to return Li Yu to his unit, but Mengrong kept him imprisoned and refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 中使再至，乃執奏曰：「臣誠知不奉詔當誅，然臣職司輦轂，合為陛下彈抑豪強。

translations.literal: When the palace envoy came again he held the memorial and said: "I truly know that not obeying the edict deserves execution, yet my office is in charge of the capital region and ought to restrain the powerful for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came a second time, Mengrong held firm and memorialized: "I know that disobeying an imperial edict deserves death, yet my duty is to govern the capital and restrain the powerful on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 錢未盡輸，昱不可得。」

translations.literal: The money has not been fully paid; Yu cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Until the debt is fully repaid, Li Yu will not be released.

sentences.zh: 上以其守正，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he upheld righteousness, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recognizing his integrity, granted the request.

sentences.zh: 自此豪右斂跡，威望大震。

translations.literal: From this the powerful drew in their steps and his authority and prestige shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the powerful curbed their conduct, and his authority resounded throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官權知禮部貢舉，頗抑浮華，選擇才藝。

translations.literal: Soon with his present office he acted provisionally in charge of the Ministry of Rites examination, quite restraining flashy display and selecting talent and skill.
translations.idiomatic: He soon assumed provisional charge of the civil service examinations, curbing flashy display and selecting candidates for genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹，亦有威名。

translations.literal: He went out as Metropolitan Prefect of Henan and also had a reputation for authority.
translations.idiomatic: Posted out as metropolitan prefect of Henan, he earned a reputation for stern authority there as well.

sentences.zh: 俄知禮部選事，征拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was in charge of Ministry of Rites selection affairs and was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of Ministry of Rites selection affairs and was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會十年六月，盜殺宰相武元衡，並傷議臣裴度。

translations.literal: It happened in the sixth month of the tenth year that bandits killed the chief minister Wu Yuanheng and also wounded the remonstrance official Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year assassins killed Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng and wounded Remonstrance Official Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 時淮夷逆命，兇威方熾，王師問罪，未有成功。

translations.literal: At the time the Huai barbarians defied orders, fierce power was just then blazing, and the royal army demanded punishment but had not yet achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai rebels were in open defiance, their power at its height, and the imperial army's punitive campaign had yet to succeed.

sentences.zh: 言事者繼上章疏請罷兵。

translations.literal: Those who spoke on affairs repeatedly submitted memorials requesting withdrawal of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists repeatedly petitioned the throne to withdraw the army.

sentences.zh: 是時盜賊竊發，人情甚惑，獨孟容詣中書雪涕而言曰：「昔漢廷有一汲黯，奸臣尚為寢謀。

translations.literal: At this time bandits arose in secret and men's hearts were greatly confused; Mengrong alone went to the Secretariat with tears streaming and said: "In former times the Han court had one Ji An, and treacherous ministers still laid their plots to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was spreading and public morale was shaken. Mengrong alone went to the Secretariat, weeping openly, and said, "In the Han dynasty a single Ji An was enough to make treacherous ministers abandon their plots.

sentences.zh: 今主上英明，朝廷未有過失，而狂賊敢爾無狀，寧謂國無人乎？

translations.literal: Now the ruler is enlightened and brilliant, the court has no faults, yet mad bandits dare to be so lawless—can it be said the state has no men?
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is enlightened, the court has committed no fault, yet these mad assassins dare such outrage. Are we to believe the empire has no capable men?

sentences.zh: 然轉禍為福，此其時也。

translations.literal: Yet to turn disaster into blessing—this is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to turn disaster into blessing—this is the moment to do it.

sentences.zh: 莫若上聞，起裴中丞為相，令主兵柄，大索賊黨，窮其奸源。」

translations.literal: Nothing is better than reporting upward, raising Vice Censor Pei to be chief minister, ordering him to hold military authority, greatly searching out the bandit faction, and exhausting the sources of their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Report to the throne, appoint Vice Censor Pei as chief minister, place military authority in his hands, hunt down the assassins' faction, and trace the conspiracy to its roots.

sentences.zh: 後數日，度果為相，而下詔行誅。

translations.literal: After several days Du indeed became chief minister, and an edict was issued to carry out executions.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Pei Du was indeed appointed chief minister, and edicts ordering executions followed.

sentences.zh: 時孟容議論人物，有大臣風彩。

translations.literal: At the time Mengrong's discussions of men had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mengrong's judgments of men displayed the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 由太常卿為尚書左丞，奉詔宣慰汴宋陳許河陽行營諸軍，俄拜東都留守。

translations.literal: From Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, received edict to console the armies of the Bian-Song, Chen-Xu, and Heyang campaign headquarters, and soon was appointed Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, he was ordered to console the armies of the Bian-Song, Chen-Xu, and Heyang campaign headquarters, and was soon appointed eastern capital garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年四月卒，年七十六，贈太子少保，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he died, aged seventy-six; he was posthumously granted Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, with posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe at the age of seventy-six, was posthumously appointed junior tutor to the crown prince, and was given the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 孟容方勁，富有文學。

translations.literal: Mengrong was square and forceful, rich in literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong was upright and forceful, and richly learned in literature.

sentences.zh: 其折衷禮法，考詳訓典，甚堅正，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: In balancing ritual and law, examining and detailing canonical instruction, he was very firm and correct, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In adjudicating ritual and law and in his careful study of canonical texts he was notably firm and correct, and commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 而又好推轂，樂善拔士，士多歸之。

translations.literal: Moreover he loved to promote the carriage of others, delighted in goodness and elevating scholars, and scholars mostly turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved to advance others, delighted in recognizing talent, and scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 呂元膺呂元膺，字景夫，鄆州東平人。

translations.literal: Lü Yuanying, Lü Yuanying, styled Jingfu, was a man of Dongping in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuanying, whose courtesy name was Jingfu, came from Dongping in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖紹宗，右拾遺。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shaozong was Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shaozong served as right reminder.

sentences.zh: 祖霈，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pei was Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pei served as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 父長卿，右衛倉曹參軍，以元膺贈秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Changqing was Right Guard Army Granary Registrar; because of Yuanying he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changqing served as registrar in the Right Guard granary office; Yuanying's honors earned him a posthumous appointment as director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元膺質度瑰偉，有公侯之器。

translations.literal: Yuanying's substance and bearing were magnificent and grand; he had the capacity of a duke or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying possessed a magnificent bearing and the makings of a statesman.

sentences.zh: 建中初，策賢良對問第，授同州安邑尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he ranked in the examination for Worthy and Good Responses to Questions and was appointed Wei of Anyi in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign he ranked in the examination for worthy and good responses and was appointed captain of Anyi in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 同州刺史侯鐈聞其名，辟為長春宮判官。

translations.literal: The Tongzhou prefect Hou Qian heard his name and summoned him as judge of the Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou Prefect Hou Qian heard of his reputation and recruited him as judge of the Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 屬浦賊侵軼，鐈失所，元膺遂潛跡不務進取。

translations.literal: When Pu bandits raided and plundered, Qian lost his post, and Yuanying thereupon went into hiding and did not strive for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu bandits raided the region, Hou Qian lost his post, and Yuanying withdrew from public life and ceased to seek advancement.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，論惟明節制渭北，延在賓席，自是名達於朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan Lun Weiming commanded Weibei and kept him at the guest seat; from this his name reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign Lun Weiming, commanding Weibei, retained him on his staff, and from that point his name reached the court.

sentences.zh: 惟明卒，王棲曜代領其鎮。

translations.literal: When Weiming died, Wang Qiyao took over command of his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun Weiming died, Wang Qiyao succeeded to command of his territory.

sentences.zh: 德宗俾棲曜留署使職，咨以軍政。

translations.literal: Dezong had Qiyao remain in provisional charge of commissioner duties and consulted him on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had Wang Qiyao retain provisional charge of the commissioner's duties and consulted him on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 累轉殿中侍御史，征入，真拜本官，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Palace Attendant Censor; he was summoned to the capital, was formally appointed to that office, and was transferred to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After serving in several posts, he rose to Palace Attendant Censor. Summoned to the capital, he received formal appointment to that rank and was then promoted to Censor.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，服闋，除右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Upon the death of his stepmother he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed Vice Director in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died, he left office to observe mourning. After the mourning period ended, he was appointed Vice Director in the Right Office of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為蘄州刺史，頗著恩信。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Qizhou, and displayed considerable benevolence and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as prefect of Qizhou, where he won a strong reputation for fairness and kindness.

sentences.zh: 嘗歲終閱郡獄囚，囚有自告者曰：「某有父母在，明日元正不得相見。」

translations.literal: Once, at year's end, he reviewed the prisoners in the prefectural jail; a prisoner who spoke up said: "I have parents alive; tomorrow is New Year's Day and I will not be able to see them."
translations.idiomatic: Once, at year's end, he reviewed the prisoners in the prefectural jail. One prisoner spoke up: "I still have parents living at home, and tomorrow is New Year's Day—I will not be able to see them.

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: and thereupon wept.
translations.idiomatic: With that he burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 元膺憫焉，盡脫其械縱之，與為期。

translations.literal: Yuanying took pity on him, removed all his fetters and released him, setting a date for return.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, Yuanying had all his shackles removed and let him go, fixing a date for his return.

sentences.zh: 守吏曰：「賊不可縱。」

translations.literal: The guarding officials said: "A criminal must not be released."
translations.idiomatic: The jail guards objected: "You cannot release a criminal.

sentences.zh: 元膺曰：「吾以忠信待之。」

translations.literal: Yuanying said: "I will treat him with loyalty and trust."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying replied: "I shall treat him with good faith.

sentences.zh: 及期，無後到者。

translations.literal: When the appointed day came, none arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, every prisoner returned on time—not one was late.

sentences.zh: 由是群盜感義，相引而去。

translations.literal: Because of this the band of criminals were moved by righteousness and led one another away.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his integrity, the other prisoners were moved to leave of their own accord, one after another.

sentences.zh: 元和初，征拜右司郎中、兼侍御史，知雜事，遷諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign, he was summoned and appointed Director in the Right Office and concurrently Censor, charged with miscellaneous affairs; he was promoted to Remonstrance and Reviewing Advisor and Attendant Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era, he was recalled to the capital and appointed Director in the Right Office of the Secretariat, with concurrent duties as Censor overseeing miscellaneous matters. He was then promoted to Remonstrance and Reviewing Advisor and Attendant Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 規諫駁議，大舉其職。

translations.literal: In remonstrating, admonishing, and rejecting proposals, he greatly fulfilled his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In remonstrance, admonition, and the review of imperial proposals, he fully discharged his responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 及鎮州王承宗之叛，憲宗將以吐突丞璀為招討處置使。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong of Zhen Prefecture rebelled, Emperor Xianzong intended to appoint Tutu Chenghuan as Pacification and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou rebelled, Emperor Xianzong planned to appoint Tutu Chenghuan as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元膺與給事中穆質、孟簡，兵部侍郎許孟容等八人抗論不可，且曰：「承璀雖貴寵，然內臣也。

translations.literal: Yuanying, together with Attendant Drafting Officers Mu Zhi and Meng Jian, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and eight others in all, argued forcefully that this was inadmissible, saying: "Although Chenghuan enjoys high favor, he is an inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying joined Attendant Drafting Officers Mu Zhi and Meng Jian, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and five others—eight men in all—in forceful opposition, arguing: "Although Chenghuan enjoys the emperor's special favor, he is a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 若為帥總兵，恐不為諸將所伏。」

translations.literal: If he is made commander-in-chief commanding troops, I fear the generals will not submit to him."
translations.idiomatic: If he is made supreme commander, I fear the field generals will refuse to follow him.

sentences.zh: 指諭明切，憲宗納之，為改使號，然猶專戎柄，無功而還。

translations.literal: Their arguments were pointed and clear; Xianzong accepted them and changed the commissioner's title, yet Chenghuan still held exclusive military authority and returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Their reasoning was clear and compelling. Xianzong accepted it and altered the commissioner's title, but Chenghuan still retained full control of the campaign—and returned without victory.

sentences.zh: 出為同州刺史，及中謝，上問時政得失，元膺論奏，辭氣激切，上嘉之。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Tong Prefecture; at his audience to thank the emperor, the emperor asked about the gains and losses of current policy, and Yuanying submitted his views—the tone was impassioned and cutting, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Tongzhou. At his audience to express thanks, the emperor asked about the strengths and failings of current policy. Yuanying's reply was forceful and blunt, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 翌日謂宰相曰：「元膺有讜言直氣，宜留在左右，使言得失，卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: The next day he said to the chief ministers: "Yuanying has forthright remonstrances and an upright spirit; he should be kept close at hand to speak of gains and losses—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor said to his chief ministers: "Yuanying speaks bluntly and holds himself upright. He ought to stay at court where he can tell me plainly what is right and wrong—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 李籓、裴垍賀曰：「陛下納諫，超冠百王，乃宗社無疆之休。

translations.literal: Li Fan and Pei Ji congratulated him, saying: "Your Majesty accepts remonstrances, surpassing all kings—a boundless blessing for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan and Pei Ji replied in praise: "Your Majesty's willingness to heed remonstrance surpasses that of every ruler of old—it is an unending blessing for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 臣等不能廣求端士，又不能數進忠言，孤負聖心，合當罪戾。

translations.literal: We your ministers have been unable broadly to seek upright men, and unable frequently to advance loyal words; we have failed Your Majesty's intent and deserve punishment.
translations.idiomatic: We have neither sought out enough upright men nor offered loyal counsel often enough. We have failed your trust and deserve blame.

sentences.zh: 請留元膺給事左右。」

translations.literal: We request that Yuanying be kept close to attend upon you."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Yuanying be kept at your side as an Attendant Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 尋兼皇太子侍讀，賜以金紫。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally appointed Reader-in-Waiting to the Crown Prince and granted gold seals and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also made Reader-in-Waiting to the Crown Prince and awarded the gold seal and purple robes of high rank.

sentences.zh: 尋拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除鄂嶽觀察使，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Observation Commissioner of E-Yue, then entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was made Observation Commissioner of Ezhou and Yuezhou, then recalled to serve as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 度支使潘孟陽與太府卿王遂叠相奏論，孟陽除散騎常侍，遂為鄧州刺史，皆假以美詞。

translations.literal: The Director of Revenue Pan Mengyang and the Director of the Palace Storehouse Wang Sui submitted memorials against each other in succession; Mengyang was appointed Regular Attendant, Sui was made Prefect of Deng Prefecture, both appointments cloaked in flattering language.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Revenue Pan Mengyang and Palace Storehouse Director Wang Sui filed successive memorials denouncing each other. Mengyang was appointed Regular Attendant, and Wang Sui was made prefect of Dengzhou—both edicts wrapped in flattering language.

sentences.zh: 元膺封還詔書，請明示枉直。

translations.literal: Yuanying sealed and returned the edicts, requesting a clear indication of who was wrong and who was right.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying returned the edicts unopened and asked that the court openly state which man was in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使裴堪奏虔州刺史李將順贓狀，朝廷不覆按，遽貶將順道州司戶。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Pei Kan memorialized on the corruption of Qian Prefecture Prefect Li Jiangshun; the court did not reinvestigate and abruptly demoted Jiangshun to Registrar of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Pei Kan reported that Qianzhou prefect Li Jiangshun was corrupt. Without reinvestigating, the court immediately demoted Jiangshun to registrar of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 元膺曰：「廉使奏刺史贓罪，不覆檢即謫去，縱堪之詞足信，亦不可為天下法。」

translations.literal: Yuanying said: "When an integrity commissioner reports a prefect's corruption, to demote and exile him without reinvestigation—even if Kan's words are fully credible—this still cannot become a standard for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying objected: "When an integrity commissioner accuses a prefect of corruption, to banish him without a follow-up investigation—even if Pei Kan's charges are entirely credible—cannot be allowed to set a precedent for the empire.

sentences.zh: 又封詔書，請發御史按問，宰臣不能奪。

translations.literal: Again he sealed and returned the edicts, requesting that censors be dispatched to investigate; the chief ministers could not override him.
translations.idiomatic: Once again he returned the edict and asked that censors be sent to conduct an inquiry—and the chief ministers could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 代權德輿為東都留守、檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、都畿防禦使。

translations.literal: He replaced Quan Deyu as Eastern Capital Administrator, Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Metropolitan Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Quan Deyu as Eastern Capital Administrator, with acting rank as Minister of Works, concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief, and command of metropolitan defenses.

sentences.zh: 舊例，留守賜旗甲，與方鎮同。

translations.literal: By old precedent, administrators were granted banners and armor, the same as regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding custom, Eastern Capital Administrators were granted military banners and armor—the same honors accorded to regional military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 及元膺受任不賜，朝論以淮西用兵，特用元膺守洛，不宜削其儀制，以沮威望，諫官論列，援華、汝、壽三州例。

translations.literal: When Yuanying took office and was not granted them, court opinion held that with warfare in Huai West, Yuanying had been specially used to guard Luoyang, and his ceremonial regalia should not be reduced lest his authority be weakened; remonstrating officials argued by citing the precedents of Hua, Ru, and Shou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanying took office without receiving them, court opinion held that because troops were engaged in Huai Xi, he had been placed in Luoyang for a special purpose—and that stripping him of these honors would undermine his authority. Remonstrating officials pressed the point, citing the precedents of Hua, Ru, and Shou prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此數處並宜不賜。」
