translations.literal: The emperor said: "All of these posts alike should not receive them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "None of these posts should receive such honors.

sentences.zh: 留守不賜旗甲，自元膺始。

translations.literal: That administrators were not granted banners and armor began with Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanying's tenure onward, Eastern Capital Administrators no longer received banners and armor.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，鄆州李師道留邸伏甲謀亂。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, Li Shidao of Yan Prefecture concealed armed men in his capital residence to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yuanhe 10, Li Shidao of Yanzhou hid armed men in his Luoyang residence to stage an uprising.

sentences.zh: 初，師道於東都置邸院，兵諜雜以往來，吏不敢辨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shidao had established a residence compound in the Eastern Capital; soldiers and spies mixed in going back and forth, and officials dared not scrutinize them.
translations.idiomatic: For some time Li Shidao had maintained a compound in Luoyang through which soldiers and spies passed freely, and local officials did not dare challenge them.

sentences.zh: 因吳元濟北犯，郊畿多警，防禦兵盡戍伊闕。

translations.literal: Because Wu Yuanji invaded northward, the capital suburbs were alarmed in many places, and the defense troops were all garrisoned at Yique.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji launched his northern offensive, the suburbs around the capital fell into widespread alarm, and all defensive forces were posted at Yique.

sentences.zh: 師道伏甲百余於邸院，將焚宮室而肆殺掠。

translations.literal: Shidao concealed more than a hundred armed men in the residence compound, intending to burn the palace buildings and carry out slaughter and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao hid more than a hundred armed men in the compound, planning to burn the palace quarters and unleash slaughter and looting across the city.

sentences.zh: 已烹牛饗眾，明日將出。

translations.literal: They had already cooked oxen to feast the crowd and would set out the next day.
translations.idiomatic: They had slaughtered cattle to feast their men and planned to strike the following day.

sentences.zh: 會小將李再興告變，元膺追兵伊闕，圍之，半月無敢進攻者。

translations.literal: As it happened, the junior officer Li Zaixing reported the plot; Yuanying pursued troops to Yique and besieged the compound, but for half a month none dared press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Then a junior officer named Li Zaixing reported the plot. Yuanying rushed troops from Yique and surrounded the compound, but for two weeks no one dared launch an assault.

sentences.zh: 防禦判官王茂元殺一人而後進。

translations.literal: The defense commissioner's aide Wang Maoyuan killed one man and only then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Defense aide Wang Maoyuan killed one rebel before he would advance.

sentences.zh: 或有毀其墉而入者，賊眾突出，圍兵奔駭。

translations.literal: When some broke through the wall to enter, the rebels burst out in force; the besieging troops fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When attackers breached the wall, the rebels surged out and the surrounding troops broke and fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 賊乃團結，以其孥偕行。

translations.literal: The rebels then banded together and took their wives and children with them as they went.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels regrouped and marched off with their families in tow.

sentences.zh: 出長夏門，轉掠郊墅，奪牛馬，東濟伊水，望山而去。

translations.literal: They went out through Changxia Gate, turned to plunder suburban estates, seized oxen and horses, crossed the Yi River eastward, and departed toward the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They fled through Changxia Gate, raided country estates along the way, seized livestock, crossed the Yi River to the east, and made for the hills.

sentences.zh: 元膺誡境上兵重購以捕之。

translations.literal: Yuanying ordered troops on the border to offer heavy rewards for their capture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying instructed border troops to post rich bounties for the rebels' capture.

sentences.zh: 數月，有山棚賣鹿於市。

translations.literal: After several months, mountain dwellers were selling deer in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Months later, hill people brought deer to sell at market.

sentences.zh: 賊過，山棚乃召集其黨，引官兵圍於谷中，盡獲之。

translations.literal: When the rebels passed by, the mountain dwellers gathered their band, led government troops to surround them in a valley, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels passed nearby, these hill dwellers rallied their allies, guided government troops into a valley ambush, and captured the entire band.

sentences.zh: 窮理其魁，乃中嶽寺僧圓凈，年八十余，嘗為史思明將，偉悍過人。

translations.literal: On thorough investigation the ringleader was found to be the monk Yuanjing of the Central Peak Temple, over eighty years old, who had once been a general under Shi Siming and surpassed others in stature and fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation revealed the ringleader to be Yuanjing, a monk of the Central Peak Temple. Over eighty years old, he had once served as a general under Shi Siming and was a man of towering build and terrifying strength.

sentences.zh: 初執之，使折其脛，錘之不折。

translations.literal: When first captured, they ordered his shins broken; they hammered but could not break them.
translations.idiomatic: Upon capture, his captors tried to break his shins with hammers—but the bones would not break.

sentences.zh: 圓凈罵曰：「腳猶不解折，乃稱健兒乎！」

translations.literal: Yuanjing cursed: "You can't even break a leg and you call yourselves brave warriors!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing spat at them: "You can't even break a man's legs and you call yourselves soldiers!

sentences.zh: 自置其足教折之。

translations.literal: He placed his own feet and taught them how to break them.
translations.idiomatic: He showed them himself—placed his feet and told them exactly how to do it.

sentences.zh: 臨刑嘆曰：「誤我事，不得使洛城流血！」

translations.literal: Facing execution, he sighed: "You have ruined my mission—I could not make Luoyang run with blood!"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground he sighed: "You have ruined everything—I never got to make Luoyang run with blood!

sentences.zh: 死者凡數十人。

translations.literal: Those who died numbered several dozen in all.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen men were put to death.

sentences.zh: 留守防禦將二人，都亭驛卒五人，甘水驛卒三人，皆潛受其職署而為之耳目，自始謀及將敗無知者。

translations.literal: Two generals of the administrator's defense command, five runners of Duting Post station, and three runners of Ganshui Post station—all had secretly received appointments from them and served as their eyes and ears; from the first planning until near defeat, none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Two defense generals under the administrator, five couriers from Duting Station, and three from Ganshui Station had all secretly accepted commissions from the rebels and served as their informants—and from the first plotting until the plot nearly collapsed, no one knew.

sentences.zh: 初，師道多買田於伊闕、陸渾之間，凡十余處，故以舍山棚而衣食之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shidao had bought much land between Yique and Luhun—more than ten places in all—so he housed mountain dwellers there and provided food and clothing for them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao had long before purchased more than a dozen estates between Yique and Luhun, housing hill people there and supporting them with food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 有訾嘉珍、門察者，潛部分之，以屬圓凈。

translations.literal: There were Zi Jiazhen and Men Cha, who secretly allocated them and placed them under Yuanjing's command.
translations.idiomatic: Two agents, Zi Jiazhen and Men Cha, secretly organized these assets and placed them under Yuanjing's command.

sentences.zh: 以師道錢千萬偽理佛寺，期以嘉珍竊發時舉火於山中，集二縣山棚人作亂。

translations.literal: Using ten million of Shidao's cash under the pretense of building a Buddhist temple, they planned that when Jiazhen launched his secret attack they would raise fire in the mountains and gather hill people of two counties to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Using ten million of Li Shidao's cash, ostensibly to build a Buddhist temple, they planned that when Jiazhen launched the surprise attack they would signal with bonfires in the mountains and muster hill dwellers from two counties to rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 及窮按之，嘉珍、門察皆稱害武元衡者。

translations.literal: When thoroughly investigated, Jiazhen and Men Cha both claimed to have been those who killed Wu Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation, both Jiazhen and Men Cha confessed to having murdered Wu Yuanheng.

sentences.zh: 元膺以聞，送之上都，賞告變人楊進、李再興錦彩三百匹、宅一區，授之郎將。

translations.literal: Yuanying reported this and sent them to the upper capital; he rewarded the informants Yang Jin and Li Zaixing with three hundred bolts of brocade and silk and one residence, and appointed them as brigade generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying reported the findings and sent the prisoners to the capital. He rewarded the informants Yang Jin and Li Zaixing with three hundred bolts of brocade and silk, a residence, and appointments as brigade generals.

sentences.zh: 無膺因請募山河子弟以衛宮城，從之。

translations.literal: Yuanying thereupon requested to recruit local youths from the mountains and rivers to guard the palace city; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying then petitioned to recruit local youths from the surrounding hills and waterways to guard the imperial city, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 盜發之日，都城震恐，留守兵寡弱，不可倚，而元膺坐皇城門，指使部分，氣意自若，以故居人帖然。

translations.literal: On the day the plot erupted, the capital was shaken with terror; the administrator's troops were few and weak and could not be relied upon, yet Yuanying sat at the imperial city gate, directing deployments with calm bearing and assured manner, and so the residents were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot broke, the capital was gripped with fear. The garrison was too small and weak to depend on, yet Yuanying took his seat at the imperial city gate, calmly directing defenses—and the people of the city settled down.

sentences.zh: 數年，改河中尹，充河中節度等使。

translations.literal: After several years, he was changed to Governor of Hezhong and served as Military Commissioner of Hezhong and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was made governor of Hezhong and Military Commissioner of the Hezhong circuit.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮多事姑息，元膺獨以堅正自處，監軍使洎往來中貴，無不敬憚。

translations.literal: At the time regional commanders mostly practiced indulgence; Yuanying alone held himself with firm uprightness, and the army supervisors and visiting inner attendants—all without exception held him in respect and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commissioners of the day were mostly given to indulgence and appeasement, but Yuanying alone conducted himself with uncompromising integrity. Army supervisors and palace eunuchs who passed through his domain all treated him with a wary respect.

sentences.zh: 入拜吏部侍郎，因疾固讓，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel; because of illness he firmly declined, and was changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Vice Minister of Personnel, but pleaded illness and firmly declined the post; he was reassigned as Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年二月卒，年七十二，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe he died, at age seventy-two; he was posthumously granted Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of Yuanhe 15, aged seventy-two, and was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元膺學識深遠，處事得體，正色立朝，有臺輔之望。

translations.literal: Yuanying's learning and knowledge were profound and far-reaching; in handling affairs he was appropriate; he maintained a stern countenance at court and had the expectations of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying was a man of deep learning and sound judgment, who handled affairs with impeccable tact. Upright and solemn at court, he seemed destined for the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 初遊京師時，故相齊映謂人曰：「吾不及識婁、郝，殆斯人之類乎！」

translations.literal: When he first traveled to the capital, the former chief minister Qi Ying said to others: "I did not get to know Lou and Hao—this may be a man of that sort!"
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived in the capital, the former chief minister Qi Ying remarked to others: "I never had the chance to know Lou and Hao—but this man may be their equal!

sentences.zh: 其業官行己，始終無缺云。

translations.literal: His achievements in office and conduct of self, from beginning to end without flaw, so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In his career and in his personal conduct, he was without reproach from first to last, or so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 劉棲楚劉棲楚，出於寒微，為吏鎮州，王承宗甚奇之。

translations.literal: Liu Qichu, Liu Qichu, came from humble origins; he served as a clerk in Zhen Prefecture, and Wang Chengzong thought him quite extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu came from a humble background. While serving as a clerk in Zhenzhou he caught the eye of Wang Chengzong, who found him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 後有薦於李逢吉，自鄧掾擢為拾遺。

translations.literal: Later someone recommended him to Li Fengji, and from Dengzhou aide he was promoted to Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone recommended him to Li Fengji, and he rose from a post in Dengzhou to Reminder at court.

sentences.zh: 性果敢。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resolute by temperament.

sentences.zh: 逢吉以為鷹犬之用，欲中傷裴度及殺李紳。

translations.literal: Fengji regarded him as useful as hawk and hound, intending to harm Pei Du and to kill Li Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji valued him as a weapon—someone to sic on his enemies—and meant to use him to destroy Pei Du and have Li Shen killed.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，畋遊稍多，坐朝常晚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, hunting and pleasure-seeking gradually increased, and he often held court late.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he spent more time hunting and at play, and often held court late in the day.

sentences.zh: 棲楚出班，以額叩龍墀出血，苦諫曰：「臣歷觀前王，嗣位之初，莫不躬勤庶政，坐以待旦。

translations.literal: Qichu stepped forth from the ranks, knocked his forehead on the imperial terrace steps until it bled, and remonstrated bitterly, saying: "Your servant has broadly observed former kings—at the beginning of their succession, none failed personally to attend diligently to common affairs, sitting until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu stepped forward from the ranks, pounding his forehead against the steps of the imperial dais until it bled, and remonstrated fiercely: "I have studied the reigns of past emperors. At the start of every new reign, the sovereign personally applied himself to governance, sitting up until dawn.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位已來，放情嗜寢，樂色忘憂，安臥宮闈，日晏方起。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, you have indulged your feelings and loved sleep, delighted in beauty and forgotten cares, lying at ease within the inner palace, and only rise when the sun is high.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, you have indulged in sleep, given yourself over to pleasure, and lain at ease within the inner palace—not rising until the sun is well up.

sentences.zh: 西宮密邇，未過山陵，鼓吹之聲，日喧於外。

translations.literal: The Western Palace is close at hand; the imperial tombs have not yet passed their mourning period, yet the sounds of drums and pipes daily clamor outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Palace lies close by, and the mourning period for the late emperor has not yet ended—yet the sound of music and revelry clamors outside every day.

sentences.zh: 伏以憲宗皇帝、大行皇帝，皆是長君，恪勤庶政，四方猶有叛亂。

translations.literal: I submit that Emperor Xianzong and the late emperor were both mature rulers who diligently attended to common affairs, yet the four quarters still had rebellions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong and the late emperor were seasoned rulers who applied themselves tirelessly to governance—and even they faced rebellions across the empire.

sentences.zh: 陛下運當少主，即位未幾，惡德布聞，臣慮福祚之不長也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's fate is that of a young ruler; you have reigned but a short time, and ill repute spreads abroad—I fear your fortune and reign will not be long.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a young ruler, and you have not long been on the throne. Ill report of your conduct is already spreading. I fear your reign will not last.

sentences.zh: 臣忝諫官，致陛下有此，請碎首以謝！」

translations.literal: Your servant disgraces the remonstrating office and has allowed Your Majesty to come to this—I beg to smash my head to atone!"
translations.idiomatic: As a remonstrating official, I am ashamed to have allowed Your Majesty to come to this. I beg leave to dash out my brains in atonement!

sentences.zh: 遂以額叩龍墀，久之不已。

translations.literal: Thereupon he knocked his forehead on the imperial terrace for a long time without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: With that he resumed pounding his forehead against the steps, and would not stop for a long while.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李逢吉出位宣曰：「劉棲楚休叩頭，候詔旨。」

translations.literal: Chief minister Li Fengji stepped forward and announced: "Liu Qichu, cease knocking your head; await the imperial decree."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Fengji stepped forward and proclaimed: "Liu Qichu, stop your kowtow and await the emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 棲楚捧首而起，因更陳論，磕頭見血。

translations.literal: Qichu held his head and rose, then again presented his arguments, knocking his head until blood showed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu lifted his bloodied head and rose, then continued his remonstrance—kowtowing until the blood ran again.

sentences.zh: 上為之動容，以袖連揮令出。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by this and repeatedly waved his sleeve ordering him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly shaken and waved him away again and again with his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 棲楚又云：「不可臣奏，臣即碎首死。」

translations.literal: Qichu again said: "If Your Majesty will not hear my memorial, your servant will immediately dash out his brains and die."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu cried out: "If Your Majesty will not hear me out, I will dash out my brains on this spot!

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎牛僧孺復宣示而出，敬宗為之動容。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Niu Sengru again announced the order for him to withdraw, and Jingzong was moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Niu Sengru again ordered him to withdraw—and even Jingzong was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 無何，遷起居郎，至諫議。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Diarist, then reached Remonstrance and Reviewing Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Diarist and then to Remonstrance and Reviewing Advisor.

sentences.zh: 俄又宣授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally appointed by edict as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, by direct imperial appointment, he was made Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 丞郎宣授，未之有也。

translations.literal: That a director or vice minister should be appointed by edict had never occurred before.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had a director- or vice-minister-level post been filled by direct edict.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹，摧抑豪右，甚有鉤距，人多比之於西漢趙廣漢者。

translations.literal: He was changed to Governor of Jingzhao, crushing and suppressing powerful families; he had considerable powers of investigation and entrapment, and many compared him to Zhao Guanghan of Western Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Jingzhao, where he cracked down hard on powerful families with fierce investigative methods. Many compared him to Zhao Guanghan of the Western Han.

sentences.zh: 後恃權寵，常以詞氣淩宰相韋處厚，遂出為桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: Later, relying on favor and authority, he often used overbearing tone toward Chief Minister Wei Chuhou, and was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, emboldened by imperial favor, he regularly spoke down to Chief Minister Wei Chuhou—and was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒於任，時大和元年九月。

translations.literal: After a year he died in his post; this was the ninth month of the first year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office, in the ninth month of Dahe 1.

sentences.zh: 張宿張宿者，布衣諸生也。

translations.literal: Zhang Su, Zhang Su, was a commoner student.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su was a commoner, a student without official rank.

sentences.zh: 憲宗為廣陵王時，因軍使張茂宗薦達，出入邸第。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was Prince of Guangling, through the army commissioner Zhang Maozong's recommendation he gained access and went in and out of the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong was still Prince of Guangling, he came to Zhang's attention through the recommendation of army commissioner Zhang Maozong and began frequenting the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 及上在東宮，宿時入謁，辯譎敢言。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, Su frequently entered to pay respects; he was eloquent, cunning, and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to the Eastern Palace, Zhang Su visited regularly—clever, sharp-tongued, and bold in counsel.

sentences.zh: 洎監撫之際，驟承顧擢，授左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the time of overseeing and instructing, he suddenly received favored promotion and was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong became regent for the throne, Zhang Su was swiftly favored and promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩數召對禁中，機事不密，貶郴州郴縣丞。

translations.literal: Because of old favor he was frequently summoned for audience within the forbidden precincts; state affairs were not kept secret, and he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Chen County in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to their old connection, he was frequently summoned for private audiences within the palace—but he could not keep secrets, and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Chenxian in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十余年征入，歷贊善大夫、左補闕、比部員外郎。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he was summoned in, passing through Mentor, Left Supplementation Censor, and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts section.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later he was recalled to court, serving in succession as Mentor, Left Supplementation Censor, and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉惡之，數於上前言其狡譎，不可保信，乃用為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Fengji hated him and repeatedly told the emperor before the throne that he was crafty and cunning and could not be trusted, and so he was used as Prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Fengji disliked him and repeatedly warned the emperor that Zhang Su was cunning and untrustworthy—so he was shipped off as prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 制下，宿自理乞留，乃追制。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Su himself presented a petition requesting to remain, and the edict was therefore withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict was issued, Zhang Su petitioned in person to stay at court—and the edict was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 上欲以為諫議大夫，逢吉奏曰：「諫議職重，當以能可否朝政者為之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint him Remonstrance and Reviewing Advisor; Fengji memorialized, saying: "The remonstrance post is weighty—it should be filled by one who can approve or reject court policy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then wished to appoint him Remonstrance and Reviewing Advisor. Li Fengji objected: "That office carries great weight—it should go to someone capable of passing judgment on court policy.

sentences.zh: 宿細人，不足以汙賢者位。

translations.literal: Su is a petty man, not sufficient to defile the post of a worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su is a petty man unworthy of a post reserved for the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 陛下必須用宿，請先去臣即可。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must employ Su, I beg that you remove me first and that will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on appointing Zhang Su, remove me from office first.

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又逢吉與裴度是非不同，上方委度討伐，乃出逢吉為劍南東川節度。

translations.literal: Moreover Fengji and Pei Du differed on right and wrong; the emperor above was entrusting Du with the punitive campaign, and so sent Fengji out as military commissioner of Jiannan East Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji and Pei Du were at odds. With the emperor entrusting the campaign to Pei Du, Fengji was posted out as military commissioner of Jiannan East Chuan.

sentences.zh: 乃用宿權知諫議大夫，俄而內使宣授。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su was employed to act provisionally as Remonstrance Counselor, and soon an inner envoy proclaimed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su was then named acting remonstrance counselor, and soon a palace envoy proclaimed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 初，宰相崔群、王涯奏曰：「諫議大夫前時亦有拔自山林、起於卒伍者，其例則少，用皆有由。

translations.literal: Earlier Chief Ministers Cui Qun and Wang Ya memorialized: "Remonstrance Counselor in former times also had those drawn from mountains and forests or raised from the ranks of soldiers; such cases were few, and appointment always had its reason.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Cui Qun and Wang Ya had earlier memorialized: "Remonstrance counselors have occasionally been drawn from reclusion or from the ranks of common soldiers, but such cases are rare and always justified by exceptional merit.

sentences.zh: 或道義彰明，不求聞達；

translations.literal: Some had their Way and righteousness brilliantly manifest and did not seek fame and advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Some possessed manifest moral authority and sought no fame;

sentences.zh: 或山林卓異，出於群萃。

translations.literal: some were outstanding in mountains and forests, rising above the assembled multitude.
translations.idiomatic: others were outstanding recluses who stood above the common run.

sentences.zh: 以此選求，是愜公議。

translations.literal: To select and seek by this was to satisfy public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments made on such grounds satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 或事跡未著，恩由一時，雖有例超升，即時議未允。

translations.literal: Or their deeds and traces were not yet manifest, favor came from a single moment—although there were precedents of sudden promotion, at the time opinion did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: When a man's record is undistinguished and favor rests on a passing whim, even if precedent allows sudden promotion, contemporary opinion will not approve.

sentences.zh: 宿本非文辭入用，望實稍輕。

translations.literal: Su originally was not brought into service through literary composition; his reputation and substance are rather light.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su was not advanced for literary talent, and his reputation is slight.

sentences.zh: 驟加不次之榮，翻恐以身為累。

translations.literal: Suddenly adding unmerited honor, I fear instead that he will become a burden to himself.
translations.idiomatic: To heap unmerited honor upon him may only bring disaster upon him.

sentences.zh: 臣等所以累有論諫，依資且與郎中，事冀適中，非於此人情有厚薄，請授職方郎中。」

translations.literal: Your subjects therefore repeatedly offered remonstrance and admonition, and according to qualification would for the time grant him Director, hoping the matter would be fitting—not that in human feeling toward this man there is thick or thin; we beg that he be appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: We have remonstrated repeatedly because we wish to appoint him by regular qualification as director in the Bureau of Appointments—a fitting rank, not from any personal bias. We beg that he receive that post.

sentences.zh: 上命如初，群等乃請權知，尋又宣援。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered as at first; Qun and the others thereupon requested provisional appointment, but soon again an envoy proclaimed the grant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held to his original decision. When Cui Qun and others asked that Zhang Su serve only provisionally, a palace envoy soon proclaimed the full appointment anyway.

sentences.zh: 宿怨執政擯己，頗加讒毀。

translations.literal: Su resented that those in power had excluded him and quite added slander and defamation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su resented the ruling faction for sidelining him and spread slander against them.

sentences.zh: 依附皇甫镈等，傷害清正之士，陰事中要，以圖進取。

translations.literal: He relied on Huangfu Bo and others, harmed upright and pure scholars, secretly worked against key figures, and schemed for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Huangfu Bo and others, attacked upright officials, plotted secretly against key figures, and schemed for advancement.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，充淄青宣慰使，至東都，暴病卒，於是正人相賀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was made Commissioner to Console Ziqing; on reaching the eastern capital he died suddenly of illness, and thereupon upright men congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was appointed commissioner to console Ziqing. He reached the eastern capital and died suddenly of illness, whereupon upright officials congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 詔贈秘書監。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously appointed him director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 熊望熊望者，登進士第。

translations.literal: Xiong Wang, Xiong Wang, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wang passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 粗有文詞，而性憸險。

translations.literal: He had rough literary talent, but his nature was crafty and dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed modest literary skill but a crafty and treacherous nature.

sentences.zh: 有口辯，往往得遊公卿間，率以大言詭意，指抉時政。

translations.literal: He had eloquence in debate and often gained access among dukes and ministers, generally using grand words and devious intent to point out and expose current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted in debate, he often gained access to the highest circles, where he used grandiloquent and devious language to criticize current policy.

sentences.zh: 既由此而得進士第，務進不已。

translations.literal: Having thereby obtained the jinshi degree, he strove for advancement without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Having won his degree through such means, he pursued advancement without cease.

sentences.zh: 而京兆尹劉棲楚以不次驟居清貫，廣樹朋黨，門庭無晝夜填委不息。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Metropolitan Prefect Liu Qichu, through unmerited sudden promotion, abruptly held a pure and eminent post, broadly planted factions, and his gate and courtyard were filled day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Prefect Liu Qichu, promoted beyond merit to a lofty post, built a vast patronage network, and his residence was thronged day and night.

sentences.zh: 望出入棲楚之門，為伺密機，陰佐計畫，人無知者。

translations.literal: Wang went in and out of Qichu's gate, spied on secret affairs, secretly assisted in planning, and no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wang frequented Liu Qichu's house, spied on confidential affairs, and secretly assisted his schemes—unknown to others.

sentences.zh: 昭湣嬉遊之隙，學為歌詩。

translations.literal: In the intervals of Emperor Zhaomin's pleasure excursions he studied composing songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Jingzong's intervals of pleasure-seeking, he took up the writing of songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士崇重，不可褻狎，乃議別置東頭學士，以備曲宴賦詩，令采卑官才堪任學士者為之。

translations.literal: Because Hanlin Academicians were honored and weighty and could not be treated familiarly, they discussed separately establishing Eastern Head Academicians to supply informal banquets and poetic composition, ordering that low-ranking officials whose talent could bear the academicianship be selected.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hanlin academicians were too august for intimate court revelry, the court proposed a separate corps of "eastern-head academicians" for informal banquets and verse-making, to be drawn from lower officials of sufficient talent.

sentences.zh: 棲楚以望名薦送，事未行而昭湣崩。

translations.literal: Qichu recommended Wang by name for submission; the matter had not been carried out when Emperor Zhaomin died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu recommended Xiong Wang by name, but before the plan could be enacted Emperor Jingzong died.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，韋處厚輔政，大去奸黨。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne Wei Chuhou assisted in government and greatly removed treacherous factions.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Wei Chuhou directed the government and purged the treacherous factions.

sentences.zh: 既逐棲楚，又詔曰：「孔門高懸百行，由至順者，其身必榮；

translations.literal: Having expelled Qichu, there was also an edict: "At Confucius's gate a hundred conducts are hung high; those who follow utmost obedience, their persons will surely be honored;
translations.idiomatic: After expelling Liu Qichu, the court issued an edict: "At Confucius's gate a hundred virtues are held in esteem; those who follow the path of utmost obedience will surely win honor;

sentences.zh: 朝廷廣設眾官，踐正途者，其道必達。

translations.literal: the court broadly establishes the multitude of offices; those who tread the upright path, their Way will surely reach fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: the court establishes many offices so that those who tread the upright path may surely attain their goal.

sentences.zh: 前鄉貢進士熊望，因緣薄伎，偷冀褻幸。

translations.literal: The former presented scholar Xiong Wang, relying on slight skill, stealthily hoped for familiar favor.
translations.idiomatic: The former presented scholar Xiong Wang, trading on slight talents, sought by stealth the emperor's intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 營居中之密職，擾惑朝經；

translations.literal: He schemed for secret posts within the inner palace and disturbed and confused court regulations;
translations.idiomatic: He schemed for secret posts within the inner palace and disturbed court governance;

sentences.zh: 鼓逼下之囂聲，因依邪隙。

translations.literal: he drummed up and pressed clamor from below and relied on wicked openings.
translations.idiomatic: he stirred up clamor among subordinates and relied on wicked patrons.

sentences.zh: 及眾議波湧，累月不寧；

translations.literal: When public discussion surged like waves, for months there was no peace;
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage surged for months without abating;

sentences.zh: 司門驗繻，累月至四。

translations.literal: the Gate Office verified passes, accumulating to four months.
translations.idiomatic: the Gate Office tallied his passes month after month until they reached four.

sentences.zh: 考覆謬妄，乃非坦途。

translations.literal: Examination and review showed error and absurdity; this was not the level road.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved his conduct absurd and improper—not the level path of public service.

sentences.zh: 朕大啟康莊，以端群望，俾示投荒之典，用正向方之流。

translations.literal: We broadly open the great highway to set aright the multitude's expectations, causing to display the precedent of casting into the wilderness and using it to correct the current flowing toward wrong.
translations.idiomatic: We open the broad highway of public service to set right the people's expectations, and now display the precedent of banishment to correct those who stray from the proper path.

sentences.zh: 可漳州司戶。」

translations.literal: He may be made Registrar of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted to registrar of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 柏耆柏耆者，將軍良器之子。

translations.literal: Bo Qi, Bo Qi, was the son of the general Liangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Qi was the son of the general Liangqi.

sentences.zh: 素負志略，學縱橫家流。

translations.literal: He from of old bore ambition and strategy and studied the school of coalition strategists.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed ambition and strategic talent and studied the coalition strategists' tradition.

sentences.zh: 會王承宗以常山叛，朝廷厭兵，欲以恩澤撫之。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Chengzong rebelled from Changshan; the court was weary of troops and wished to soothe him with favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled at Changshan, the court, weary of war, wished to win him back through grace and favor.

sentences.zh: 耆於蔡州行營以畫幹裴度，請以朝旨奉使鎮州，乃自處士授左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the Caizhou campaign headquarters Qi by plan persuaded Pei Du and requested to go on imperial commission as envoy to Zhenzhou; he was thereupon appointed from Recluse to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: At the Caizhou campaign headquarters Bo Qi persuaded Pei Du through stratagem and volunteered to carry imperial orders to Zhenzhou. He was appointed from private scholar to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 既見承宗，以大義陳說。

translations.literal: After he saw Chengzong he set forth the great principles.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Wang Chengzong, he expounded the principles of loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 承宗泣下，請質二男，獻兩郡，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chengzong wept, requested to offer his two sons as hostages and present two commanderies, and thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong wept, offered his two sons as hostages and surrendered two commanderies, and Bo Qi thereby won renown.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，王承宗歸國，移鎮滑州，朝廷賜成德軍賞錢一百萬貫，令諫議大夫鄭覃宣慰軍人，賞錢未至，浩浩然騰口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe Wang Chengzong returned to allegiance, was transferred to command Huazhou, and the court granted the Chengde army reward money of one million strings of cash, ordering Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Tan to console the troops; the reward money had not arrived and voices rose in vast uproar.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe Wang Chengzong submitted to the throne and was transferred to Huazhou. The court granted the Chengde army a reward of one million strings of cash and sent Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Tan to console the troops. Before the money arrived, angry voices rose throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 穆宗詔耆往諭旨。

translations.literal: Muzong ordered Qi to go and proclaim the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong ordered Bo Qi to proclaim the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 耆至，令承宗集三軍，宣導上旨，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: When Qi arrived he ordered Chengzong to assemble the three armies, proclaimed and guided the emperor's intent, and the hearts of the masses were then calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Qi arrived, had Chengzong assemble the entire army, proclaimed the emperor's message, and restored calm.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 太和初，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was promoted to Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he was promoted to remonstrance counselor.

sentences.zh: 俄而，李同捷叛，兩河籓帥加兵滄、德，宿師於野連年。

translations.literal: Soon Li Tongjie rebelled; the Hebei military commissioners added troops at Cang and De, and troops were stationed in the field year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Tongjie rebelled. The Hebei military commissioners massed troops against Cangzhou and Dezhou, and imperial armies campaigned in the field for years.

sentences.zh: 同捷窮蹙求降。

translations.literal: Tongjie, pressed to extremity, sought to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjie, driven to desperation, sought to surrender.

sentences.zh: 耆既宣諭訖，與節度使李祐謀。

translations.literal: After Qi had finished proclaiming and instructing, he plotted with the military commissioner Li You.
translations.idiomatic: After proclaiming the surrender terms, Bo Qi plotted with Military Commissioner Li You.

sentences.zh: 耆乃帥數百騎入滄州，取同捷赴京。

translations.literal: Qi thereupon led several hundred horsemen into Cangzhou, took Tongjie, and escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Qi then led several hundred horsemen into Cangzhou, seized Tongjie, and escorted him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 滄、德平。

translations.literal: Cang and De were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou and Dezhou were pacified.

sentences.zh: 諸將害耆邀功，爭上表論列。

translations.literal: The generals resented Qi for seizing merit and vied in submitting memorials setting forth arguments.
translations.idiomatic: The generals resented Bo Qi for stealing their glory and competed in memorializing accusations against him.

sentences.zh: 文宗不獲已，貶循州司戶判官，沈亞之貶虔州南康尉。

translations.literal: Wenzong had no choice; Qi was demoted to Registrar Adjutant of Xunzhou, and Shen Yazhi was demoted to Wei of Nankang in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong had no choice but to demote Bo Qi to registrar adjutant of Xunzhou and Shen Yazhi to captain of Nankang in Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 內官馬國亮又奏耆於同捷處取婢九人，再命長流愛州，尋賜死。

translations.literal: The inner official Ma Guoliang again memorialized that Qi at Tongjie's place had taken nine maidservants; he was again ordered to distant exile in Aizhou, and soon was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Ma Guoliang further reported that Bo Qi had taken nine maidservants from Tongjie's household. He was banished to Aizhou and soon ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：人臣事君，犯顏匡政，不避死亡之誅。

translations.literal: The historiographer says, the historiographer says: When ministers serve their ruler, violating countenance to correct government, they do not avoid the punishment of death.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: When a minister serves his ruler, to remonstrate face to face and correct policy is to risk death without flinching.

sentences.zh: 議者以為徇名，臣惡其訐也。

translations.literal: Discussants consider this to be courting fame; this subject detests their contentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Critics call such conduct mere fame-seeking, but this writer detests their carping.

sentences.zh: 如許京兆之劾軍吏，呂尚書之封詔書，詞義可觀，聳動人聽，以為沽激，傷善何多！

translations.literal: Such as the Metropolitan Prefect Xu's impeachment of army officers and the Minister Lü's sealing of edicts—their words and meaning are worth viewing, startling to men's hearing; to consider them self-promotion—how much harm to goodness!
translations.idiomatic: When the metropolitan prefect Xu impeached army officers, or when Minister Lü sealed back edicts—their language was compelling and stirred the listener. To dismiss such acts as self-promotion does great injury to true public virtue!

sentences.zh: 而棲楚、張宿之徒，鷹犬下材，為人鳴吠，誠可醜也。

translations.literal: But Liu Qichu, Zhang Su, and their kind—base material of hawk and hound, barking for others—are truly detestable.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Qichu, Zhang Su, and their like were base creatures fit only to yap for their masters—truly despicable.

sentences.zh: 柏耆恃縱橫之算，欲俯拾卿相，忘身蹈利，旋踵而誅，宜哉！

translations.literal: Bo Qi relied on coalition strategists' calculations, wished to stoop and pick up the posts of chief minister and counselor, forgot his person and trod toward profit, and within a turning of the heel was executed—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Bo Qi trusted in stratagems, hoped to scoop up the highest offices at a stride, threw himself into profit, and was executed within the turning of a heel—as he deserved!

sentences.zh: 巢父使不辱命，誌在致君，遭罹喪亂，竟陷虎吻。

translations.literal: Chaofu as envoy did not disgrace his commission; his aim was to bring his ruler to perfection; he encountered disorder and ruin and in the end fell into the tiger's jaws.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu as envoy did not disgrace his mission; his aim was to serve his ruler faithfully. Caught in rebellion and chaos, he fell at last into the tiger's maw.

sentences.zh: 而戣、戢諸子，世載忠貞，大中之後，郁為昌族。

translations.literal: But Wei, Ji, and the sons of their lineage, generation after generation bore loyal fidelity; after Dazhong they flourished as a prosperous clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kong Wei, Kong Ji, and their descendants bore loyalty through generations, and after the Dazhong reign flourished as a great and honorable house.

sentences.zh: 為善之利，豈虛言哉！

translations.literal: The profit of doing good—how could it be empty words!
translations.idiomatic: The rewards of doing good are no empty saying!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君子重義，小人殉利。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The gentleman values righteousness; the petty man dies for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The gentleman values righteousness; the petty man dies for profit.

sentences.zh: 巢殞耆誅，其道即異。

translations.literal: Chaofu perished and Qi was executed—their Ways were immediately different.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu perished and Bo Qi was executed—their paths could not have been more different.

sentences.zh: 許、呂封駁，照耀黃扉。

translations.literal: Xu and Lü sealed and rejected edicts, illuminating the yellow inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Lü who sealed back edicts shine at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 死而可作，吾誰與歸？

translations.literal: Dead yet able to act—with whom shall I return?
translations.idiomatic: Though dead they still stand as exemplars—with whom shall I now keep company?
